logline: A mild-mannered Japanese salaryman kidnapped by Southeast Asian mercenary pirates decides not to go home - trading a corporate desk for a PT boat and a crew who settle disputes with bullets.

renewal.note: The two-season TV anime and the Roberta's Blood Trail OVA (2010-2011) complete the animated adaptation. The source manga by Rei Hiroe continues publication on a very irregular schedule; no new anime announced.

bollymeter.basis: MAL score of 8.04 from 538,218 users; praised for its genre energy, morally grey ensemble, and Revy's character as a rare female action lead in anime who is written without softening her violence.

seasons.review_body: The first season of Black Lagoon aired in spring 2006 and delivered exactly what Rei Hiroe's manga promised: operatic crime action staged in the fictional Southeast Asian port of Roanapur, a city where every faction - Russian mafia, Colombian cartel, Chinese Triad, neo-Nazis - has territorial claims and none has the moral high ground. Madhouse's animation gave the gun choreography a kinetic clarity that distinguished it from contemporaries. But the critical conversation clustered less on the action than on the cast dynamic: Revy, voiced by Megumi Toyoguchi in Japanese, is a rare action-anime female lead built entirely around capacity for violence rather than gender-coded softening, and the show never apologizes for her. Rock's transformation from passive hostage to willing participant provided the ethical throughline. The MAL audience score of 8.04 from over 500,000 users reflects enduring appreciation.

episode_reviews.title: The Black Lagoon
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the premise with brisk economy: salaryman Rock is kidnapped, discovers his company has written him off as acceptable collateral, and begins recalculating what loyalty means. Revy shoots things. The show knows exactly what it is from the first act.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rock's discovery that his corporate employer has abandoned him mid-kidnapping - the moment the series locates its actual subject, which is not piracy but the question of what a man owes a system that would sacrifice him.

episode_reviews.title: Rasta Blasta
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series' first multi-episode arc - the El Baile de la Muerte storyline begins here, introducing the Lovelace family and a kidnapping job that escalates well beyond the Lagoon Company's typical parameters. The arc is where the show begins testing its ensemble against stakes with genuine moral weight.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Garcia Lovelace's insistence on finding Roberta sets up the arc's central irony: the person he is trying to rescue may be more dangerous than the people holding him.

bollymeter.basis: The Second Barrage is generally rated above Season 1 by fans; the Hansel and Gretel arc in particular is cited as the darkest and most critically discussed content in the anime's run.

seasons.review_body: The Second Barrage aired immediately following Season 1 in October 2006 and pushed the franchise into significantly darker territory with the Hansel and Gretel arc - a storyline about two child assassins that the fanbase still identifies as the high point of the anime adaptation. Madhouse maintained the first season's action quality while the writing leaned harder into the moral vacuum of Roanapur as a setting. The arc's treatment of child soldiers and institutional violence was uncompromising and generated the most critical discussion of any content in the series. The second half of the season returned to the Lovelace storyline from Season 1 for its most extended multi-episode arc. Fan reception places The Second Barrage above the first season as the more ambitious of the two.
seasons.season_over_season: The Second Barrage darkens the tone considerably from Season 1; the Hansel and Gretel arc is where Black Lagoon's moral seriousness overtakes its genre pleasures.

episode_reviews.title: Swan Lake - Death Row
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opening episodes of the Hansel and Gretel arc introduce two child assassins whose backstory the show withholds strategically, using their inexplicable behavior to build dread before the explanation makes it worse. Among the most discussed episodes in the series for its handling of violence and victimhood.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first scene with Hansel and Gretel in the hotel room, where the show signals immediately that this arc will operate by different rules than anything that preceded it.
